description:
Redwood Inference is expanding its cost-optimization automation (batching, caching, quantization profiles, routing knobs) to support a safer operational workflow: every optimization config change must be versioned, validated, and reversible via one-click rollback. The project (“Safe apply + rollback mechanism”) implements (1) config versioning with immutable history, (2) a safe-apply workflow that performs preflight validation and produces a diff/preview, (3) one-click rollback to any prior known-good version, and (4) auditability and guardrails appropriate for enterprise customers (Hosted, Dedicated, and Private).

Goals:
- Prevent customer-impacting regressions caused by optimization configuration changes (e.g., overly aggressive batching/quantization leading to latency spikes, error-rate increases, or quality drops).
- Provide rapid mitigation: rollback should be executable by on-call/SRE and authorized operators within minutes.
- Improve change visibility: who changed what, when, where applied (region/cluster/customer), and why (linked ticket).
- Support progressive delivery for config changes: optional canary apply and metric gates (latency/error/SLO + quality/eval signals where applicable).

In-scope:
- Data model for config versions (per route/model/customer deployment scope) with metadata (author, source, reason, links).
- Console workflow: view history, compare versions, safe-apply wizard, rollback button, and status/health feedback.
- API endpoints to list versions, create/apply a new version, and rollback.
- Runtime/config propagation integration: ensuring atomicity and consistent rollout semantics (including cache invalidation and scheduler/batching toggles).
- Audit logging and RBAC: restrict rollback/apply permissions; log every attempt and outcome.
- SRE runbooks and incident hooks (incident-bot/deploy-bot notifications).

Out of scope (initial release):
- Fully automated rollback based on quality regressions without human confirmation (may be a follow-on).
- Arbitrary “partial rollback” of only some fields; initial version is whole-config rollback (with documented exceptions).

Stakeholders and roles:
- Product: Marissa Cole (Console & Rollouts), Paula Mendes (rollout/telemetry requirements), Aditya Rao (Optimize).
- Engineering (Console/Platform): Dylan Brooks (Console & Tooling), Chloe Martin (Console Backend), Jada Williams (rollout primitives), Felix Schneider/Hannah Rivera (implementation).
- Runtime: Mateo Alvarez (Runtime), Sofia Ivanova (Scheduling/batching behavior), Noah Patel/Omar El‑Sayed (correctness & runtime hooks).
- SRE/Infra: Neha Kapoor/Sean Gallagher (reliability), Rafael Mendes (on-call), Allison Grant (observability standards).
- Release/QA: Connor O’Brien (release train), Leila Farouk (E2E automation).
- Security Ops: Fiona McCarthy (audit/compliance expectations).

Timeline (proposed):
- Phase 0 (1–2 weeks): incident-driven requirements + PRD, choose storage/versioning strategy, define RBAC/audit events.
- Phase 1 (3–5 weeks): implement backend version store + APIs + basic Console history/rollback UI; add audit logs.
- Phase 2 (2–4 weeks): safe-apply preflight validation, diff preview, canary apply + metric gates, E2E tests.
- Phase 3 (1–2 weeks): hardening, runbooks, release notes, staged rollout (internal -> Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private).

Key constraints:
- Must be compatible with high-volume config churn while keeping read paths low-latency.
- Rollback must be safe under partial propagation/failure modes and must not create config “split brain.”
- Enterprise audit/compliance expectations: immutable history, strong access controls, and retention.

Deliverables:
- Confluence design + ADRs, runbooks, audit event spec.
- Linear project with epics/subtasks.
- GitHub PRs implementing store/API/UI/runtime hooks/tests.
- Slack coordination threads, on-call/incident threads validating rollback under pressure.
- A small number of customer-facing artifacts (support tickets, sales/security deep dives) showing why the feature matters.

files.description: Product Requirements Doc: user personas (SRE, platform operator, customer admin), workflows (safe apply, rollback, diff/preview), success metrics (reduced MTTR, change failure rate), rollout plan, and non-goals.

Technical design: version store schema, APIs, consistency model, propagation to runtime, idempotency/locking, failure modes, and integration points with routing/batching/caching/quantization profile systems.
ADR documenting the chosen storage backend (e.g., Postgres/Dynamo), immutable version semantics, whole-config rollback decision, and trade-offs vs patch-based rollback.

Runbook for on-call: how to identify a bad optimization config, verify impact via dashboards, execute one-click rollback, validate recovery, and communicate status; includes common pitfalls and escalation paths.
Operational playbook: using safe-apply preflight checks (schema validation, capacity guardrails, perf risk heuristics), interpreting warnings, and using canary apply + metric gates.
Audit log event taxonomy: apply_attempted/applied/failed, rollback_attempted/rolled_back/failed, who/what/where, request ids, and retention/redaction rules.
Private deployment considerations: how version history is stored/retained in customer environments, upgrade/migration notes, and offline/air-gapped constraints.
Known issues and mitigations: rollback interactions with KV cache, continuous batching, quantization profile swaps, and warmup behavior; includes recommended safe defaults.
Top-level Linear initiative/project issue: scope, milestones, cross-team dependencies, rollout stages (internal -> Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private), and launch criteria.
Implement DB schema for config versions, metadata, and retention; includes migration plan and backfill of current live configs as version v0.
Backend API endpoints for version listing, retrieval, diff payload generation, pagination, and filtering by scope (customer/region/model/route).
Rollback endpoint: authorization, optimistic concurrency controls, idempotency keys, and audit events; includes error handling for partial propagation.
Preflight validator: schema checks, guardrails (batch size bounds, cache toggle constraints), compatibility with quantization profiles, and dry-run propagation simulation.
Console UI work: version timeline, compare modal, metadata display (author, linked ticket), and deep links to audit log entries.
Console rollback UX: confirmation, blast-radius display, status/progress indicators, and post-rollback validation checklist.
Runtime integration: ensure config apply/rollback uses atomic update semantics per scope; define lock/lease behavior to prevent concurrent applies.
Add metrics: config_apply_latency, success/failure counters, rollback counters, and correlation ids; create alerts for elevated failure rate and stuck rollouts.
E2E automation: create version, safe-apply with preflight, canary apply, forced failure scenario, rollback, and assertion of audit log + runtime state.
RBAC additions: new permissions (optimize.config.apply, optimize.config.rollback), role mapping, and secure defaults for enterprise tenants.
PR: introduce config version store tables/models and initial API scaffolding; includes basic unit tests and feature flag wiring.
PR: implement list/get endpoints with pagination/filtering and response shapes needed by Console; adds integration tests.
PR: one-click rollback API, idempotency keys, concurrency checks, and audit log emission; includes failure-mode tests.
PR: preflight validation rules, dry-run checks, and diff generation; includes guardrails for batching/caching/quantization changes.
PR: runtime-side locking/lease mechanism for apply/rollback and status reporting back to control plane; includes metrics instrumentation.
PR: Console backend endpoints to power version history and compare view; includes caching and permission checks.
PR: rollback flow integration, async progress tracking, and notifications to Slack/on-call channels via internal hooks.
PR: canary apply support with metric gates (p95 latency, error rate); defines default thresholds and override policy.
PR: new dashboards and panels correlating config version changes with latency/error/cost metrics; adds alert rules for stuck applies.
PR: incident-bot enhancements to post config-change events, include rollback deep links, and capture correlation ids in incident channels.
PR: Helm updates for deploying the versioning/validator components, including secret management and environment-specific toggles.
PR: Private installer upgrade step adding migrations/backups for config version store; includes rollback procedure documentation.
PR: external docs draft for enterprise admins describing config history, rollback, RBAC, and audit logs (with screenshots stubs).
Thread coordinating initial architecture choices (store backend, version keys/scope), with @mentions across Console, Runtime, and SRE; includes open questions and action items.
Thread discussing PRD details: UX expectations for one-click rollback, customer-facing wording, and whether rollback should be gated by permission + justification.
Thread on runtime implications of rolling back batching/caching knobs; includes concerns about cache invalidation and warmup behavior.
Thread defining operational SLOs for config apply/rollback, desired MTTR targets, and alerting thresholds for failed/stuck applies.
Thread on RBAC and audit logging requirements; what events must be immutable, what fields can be redacted, and retention expectations for enterprise.
Thread planning phased rollout (internal -> hosted sandbox -> prod), coordinating with release train and feature flags.
Thread reviewing ADR draft and debating whole-config vs patch rollback; includes final decision and request to document edge cases.
Incident coordination thread (config-related regression) used as motivation: latency spike after optimization tweak, manual mitigation, and explicit need for faster rollback.
On-call thread: step-by-step manual rollback attempts (before feature exists), links to dashboards, and follow-up tasks for the new rollback mechanism.
Thread about implementing idempotency and concurrency control; includes example request ids and discussion of failure semantics.
Thread about diff/preview format (what fields to show, how to render nested config), and PM feedback on usability.
Thread on safe default bounds for batching parameters and how validator should consider model/context length distributions.
Thread defining metric gates for canary apply (p95 latency, error rate, saturation); includes proposed thresholds per tier.
Thread coordinating E2E test plan with QA automation; includes flakiness concerns and staging environment requirements.
Thread reviewing Console rollback UX copy (confirmation text, blast radius), with accessibility/usability comments.
Thread on updating runbooks and training on-call; includes checklist for validating rollback success and comms templates.
Announcement thread: internal beta launch of config version history and rollback; includes how to request access and where to file bugs.
Working doc: iterative notes, open questions, API sketches, and links to Linear tickets/PRs; less polished than Confluence.
Product working doc: rough wireframe notes, UI copy drafts, and decision log for history/compare/rollback screens.
Sheet-style table: proposed canary gate thresholds by environment/tier, mapping to SLOs and error budgets.
Testing matrix: scenarios for toggling batching/caching/quantization parameters, expected runtime behavior, and validation steps.
Release checklist: feature flags, migration steps, monitoring dashboards, rollback plan for the rollback feature itself, and sign-off list.
Customer support ticket: report of latency spike after an Optimize recommendation applied; investigation notes, workaround, and linkage to upcoming rollback feature.
Customer ticket: enterprise asks for audit log evidence of config changes (who/when/what) and rollback actions; includes compliance context.
Customer ticket: Dedicated tenant can’t see rollback UI due to RBAC/flag mismatch; triage, fix, and follow-up tasks.
Internal helpdesk ticket: request to add/update role mappings so SRE on-call can perform rollback in prod while limiting broader access.
Technical deep dive transcript with an enterprise prospect: need for safe config rollouts, audit logging, rollback controls; includes next steps and security questions.
CS-led call transcript after a config-related incident: customer expectations for rollback time, visibility, and change approvals.
Email thread: enterprise security stakeholder asks for audit log semantics and RBAC details; Marissa/Console team coordinate response and artifacts.
Internal email thread: Dylan + release engineering coordinate feature flag strategy, staged rollout, and mitigation plan.
Internal email thread: SRE leadership sets MTTR targets, asks for runbook completeness, and requests dashboards/alerts before GA.
HubSpot company record (enterprise): notes emphasize audit logging, rollback controls, and change management; links to Fireflies meeting and Gmail threads.
HubSpot company record (mid-market): cost sensitivity and desire for safe optimization toggles; references a prior latency regression and need for easy rollback.
